mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of GDPC1 YoY < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of UNRATE > 6.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO below 90 for two consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during INDPRO < 90 for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in UNRATE above 6% and a fall in PAYEMS below its 12-month moving average signals labor market imbalances, which increase cost pressures and reduce hiring, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS < 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in HOUST above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals rising housing demand, which correlates with increased consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when HOUST > 12-month moving average for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated fall in both FEDFUNDS and RSAFS below their respective 12-month averages signals a loosening of monetary and credit conditions, which stimulates borrowing and investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during coordinated declines in FEDFUNDS and RSAFS below their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in GDPC1 above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a robust demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when GDPC1 is above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months.
